A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain 27 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Full text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to first-page author and version information.

before.justification: v3 reports original results from 356 dialogues across 89 director–matcher pairs, participant surveys, and follow-up AI–AI experiments, with additional analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original dialogue experiments, participant survey results, follow-up AI–AI experiments, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The model procedures, dialogue-history inputs, prompt scaffolding, and structured outputs in Section 4.3 and Appendix E are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English basket-matching task, human/AI participant populations, and referring-expression validation corpus. No task or data coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The human/AI comparison conditions and evaluated GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro, and Claude Opus-4.5 pairings are unchanged, including comparator membership in Table 2.

E3.justification: Participant filtering, pair counts, the four-round design, evaluation metrics, and follow-up prompt and reasoning settings are unchanged in Sections 4 and 6 and the appendices.

E4.justification: Both retain the same prompt and reasoning analyses, mixed-model experiments, dialogue case studies, metric correlations, and extraction validation in Section 6 and Appendices B–D.

E5.justification: Figure 2's 95% confidence intervals, Table 1's significance reporting, reported standard deviations, and the follow-up limit of up to two runs per condition are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are identical throughout, including Figure 2 and Tables 1–8. For example, Table 2's default accuracy remains 92.2, 90.1, 84.4, and 76.6 across the four rounds.

T1.justification: The referring-expression length and relative lexical-overlap definitions in Section 4.5 and the mathematics in Appendix C are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about human versus LVLM grounding, the factorial study's contribution, and the corpus release.

C2.justification: Interpretations of verbosity, failed entrainment, and communication errors are unchanged, as are the limitations concerning English, basket stimuli, proprietary models, extraction proxies, and prompting.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, reasoning settings, full prompts, participant instructions, extraction details, and corpus/code access information are unchanged, including the appendix disclosures.

R1.justification: The background, related-work discussion, and bibliography are identical. No cited work or substantive positioning relative to prior research changes.

P1.justification: Page 1 changes 'Susan Brennan' to 'Susan E. Brennan' and updates the arXiv stamp from v3 dated 20 April 2026 to v4 dated 15 June 2026. Body prose, headings, references, and appendix text are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–27 are identical; page 1 differs only in author/version text, without document reflow.

improvement.justification: v4 adds an author's middle initial and updates version information. Scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation—including all appendices—remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
